reports.title: Rockwell Automation Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2026 Results; Introduces Fiscal 2027 Guidance

guidance.heading: •Fiscal 2027 guidance
section: ◦Reported sales growth of 4.5% to 7.5%; organic sales growth of 6% to 9%
MILWAUKEE (November 5, 2026) – Rockwell Automation, Inc. (NYSE: ROK) today reported fiscal 2026 fourth quarter and full year results and introduced fiscal 2027 guidance.

"Rockwell delivered a strong finish to a great year, with broad-based topline growth, margin expansion, and double-digit earnings growth. Our results underscore the differentiation of our strategy and operating model, as we continue to gain share, strengthen our leadership in core markets, and expand our position in high-growth areas including semiconductor and data centers,” said Blake Moret, Chairman and CEO.

desk.headline: Sales up 1% to $2.33bn, missed; adjusted EPS of $3.88 beat; fiscal 2027 outlook set at $14.50–15.50

other.label: Organic sales growth
other.change: cut ~4 pts by tariff refunds to customers

results: Quarterly sales rose 1% to $2.33bn (organic +3%); an $85m accrual for tariff refunds to customers cut growth by about 4 points.
Adjusted EPS rose 16% to $3.88 and diluted EPS to $3.11; both include an 11c net benefit from tariff refunds.
Software & Control grew 15% with a 34.0% margin; Intelligent Devices grew 5%; Lifecycle Services fell 9% after a divestiture.
Full-year sales rose 8% to $8.99bn, adjusted EPS rose 27% to $13.42 and free cash flow was $1.70bn.
Bought back $500m of shares in the quarter and $1.25bn for the year.

guidance.summary: First outlook for fiscal 2027: reported sales growth of 4.5–7.5% (organic 6–9%) and adjusted EPS of $14.50–15.50, with a tax rate of about 20%.

points: Semiconductor and data-centre customers were strong: semiconductor sales up about 50% and the combined area expected to grow mid-teens in fiscal 2027.
Management expects about 3 points of price in fiscal 2027, double this year, with memory and electronic component costs still rising.
Recurring revenue (ARR) growth slowed to 5% due to project delays; management targets about 7% next year.
Fiscal 2027 plan assumes an enterprise margin of about 23% and share buybacks cut to about $600m from $1.25bn.
Tariff uncertainty is weighing on car-maker customers; mining and Latin America were weak.
